ctx.x: all of a sudden." Morehouse met his wife, Evelyn, in 1924 when he was supposed to be preparing to enter the Boston Conservatory of Music, his father's idea. "I was supposed to enter in September," Morehouse said. "I had my choice, marry Evelyn and play jazz music or put it off, study theory and harmony. And we got married in August. That settled it."

The Morehouses have two children, James 19 and Suzanne 15. "When Jimmy came along, I knew I'd have to settle down," Morehouse said. "I'd been in radio since 1928 and I hadn't made up my mind to stay. That clinched it." He's been in radio orchestras ever since. At present he plays in the studio orchestras of the NBC programs, the City Service Band, Break the Bank and the Sunday Longine Hour. As for the newest fad in popular music, bebop, Morehouse hasn't a great deal of love for it. "There are always fads in the arts," he said, "and in our music bop is the latest.
